slot.brief: Given the equation of a progressive wave y = A sin(kx − ωt), ask the student to read off amplitude, frequency, wavelength and wave speed.

stem: The equation of a progressive wave is y = 0.05 sin(4 pi t - 2 pi x), where x and y are in metres and t is in seconds. Which option gives the amplitude, frequency, wavelength and wave speed of the wave?

verdicts.working: Compare with y=A sin(ωt−kx): A=0.05 m, f=ω/(2π)=2 Hz, λ=2π/k=1 m, and v=fλ=2 m/s.

working:
Compare y = A sin(omega t - kx). A = 0.05 m, omega = 4 pi rad/s, so f = omega/(2 pi) = 2 Hz. k = 2 pi m^-1, so lambda = 2 pi/k = 1 m. v = omega/k = 4 pi/(2 pi) = 2 m/s.

Independent check: Compare with y=A sin(ωt−kx): A=0.05 m, f=ω/(2π)=2 Hz, λ=2π/k=1 m, and v=fλ=2 m/s.
solution: Comparing with $y=A\sin(\omega t-kx)$, we get $A=0.05\,\text{m}$, $\omega=4\pi\,\text{rad s}^{-1}$ and $k=2\pi\,\text{m}^{-1}$.\n$$f=\frac{\omega}{2\pi}=2\,\text{Hz},\qquad \lambda=\frac{2\pi}{k}=1\,\text{m},\qquad v=f\lambda=2\,\text{m s}^{-1}.$$
